arxiv-1811-02430.title: Energy scale of nematic ordering in the parent iron-based superconductor:BaFe 2 As 2
arxiv-1811-02430.creator: Alexander Fedorov, Alexander Yaresko, Erik Haubold, Yevhen Kushnirenko, Timur Kim, Bernd Büchner, Saicharan Aswartham, Sabine Wurmehl, Sergey Borisenko
arxiv-1811-02430.description: Abstract Nematicity plays an important role in the physics of iron-based superconductors (IBS). Its microscopic origin and in particular its importance for the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity itself are highly debated. A crucial knowledge in this regard is the degree to which the nematic order influences the electronic structure of these materials.

arxiv-2006-01359.description: Abstract Predecir una crisis epiléptica, significa la capacidad de determinar de antemano el momento de una crisis con la mayor precisión posible. Un pronóstico correcto de un evento epiléptico en aplicaciones clínicas es un problema típico en procesamiento de señales biomédicas, lo cual ayuda a un diagnóstico y tratamiento apropiado de esta enfermedad.

arxiv-2006-08316.description: Abstract . We develop an algebraic language theory based on the notion of an Eilenberg–Moore algebra. arxiv-2201-08977.creator: Han Hu, Xinrong Liang, Yulin Ding, Xuekun Yuan, Qisen Shang, Bo Xu, Xuming Ge, Min Chen, Ruofei Zhong, Qing Zhu
arxiv-2201-08977.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Han Hu, Xinrong Liang, Yulin Ding, Xuekun Yuan, Qisen Shang, Bo Xu, Xuming Ge, Min Chen, Ruofei Zhong, Qing Zhu. Deep learning methods are notoriously data-hungry and requires many labeled samples. Unfortunately, the interactive sample labeling efforts have dramatically hindered the application of deep learning methods, especially for the 3D modeling tasks, which require heterogeneous samples. This paper proposes a semi-supervised adversarial recognition strategy embedded in the inverse procedural modeling to alleviate the work of data annotation for the learned 3D modeling of façades.

However, their reliance on reactions from the US Patent Office results in a lack of interpretable predictions and limited generalization capability to other chemistry domains, such as radical and atmospheric chemistry.

arxiv-2408-04343.title: Sparse Spiking Neural-like Membrane Systems on Graphics Processing Units
arxiv-2408-04343.creator: Javier Hernández-Tello 1, Miguel Á. Martínez-del-Amor 1, David Orellana-Martín 1, Francis George C. Cabarle 1,2
arxiv-2408-04343.description: Abstract The parallel simulation of Spiking Neural P systems is mainly based on a matrix representation, where the graph inherent to the neural model is encoded in an adjacency matrix. The simulation algorithm is based on a matrix-vector multiplication, which is an operation efficiently implemented on parallel devices.

arxiv-2410-08371.title: Merging in a Bottle: Differentiable Adaptive Merging (DAM) and the Path from Averaging to Automation
arxiv-2410-08371.creator: Thomas Gauthier-Caron, Shamane Siriwardhana, Elliot Stein, Malikeh Ehghaghi, Charles Goddard, Mark McQuade, Jacob Solawetz, Maxime Labonne
arxiv-2410-08371.description: Abstract By merging models, AI systems can combine the distinct strengths of separate language models, achieving a balance between multiple capabilities without requiring substantial retraining. However, the integration process can be intricate due to differences in training methods and fine-tuning, typically necessitating specialized knowledge and repeated refinement.

arxiv-2503-20750.title: Optimal Scaling Laws for Efficiency Gains in a Theoretical Transformer-Augmented Sectional MoE Framework
arxiv-2503-20750.creator: Soham Sane
arxiv-2503-20750.description: Abstract This paper introduces a theoretical framework for a Transformer-augmented, sectional Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture that aims to enhance computational efficiency while preserving model scalability. Unlike conventional MoE models, which route entire token embeddings to selected experts, our approach partitions the embedding dimension itself—assigning segments of each token’s representation to dedicated experts.

pmc-10574109.title: Synthesis of Liquid Hydrocarbon via Direct Hydrogenation of CO2 over FeCu-Based Bifunctional Catalyst Derived from Layered Double Hydroxides
pmc-10574109.creator: Ziqin Li, Kangzhou Wang, Yaqin Xing, Wenlong Song, Xinhua Gao, Qingxiang Ma, Tiansheng Zhao, Jianli Zhang
pmc-10574109.description: Here, we report a Na-promoted FeCu-based catalyst with excellent liquid hydrocarbon selectivity and catalytic activity. The physiochemical properties of the catalysts were comprehensively characterized by various characterization techniques. The characterization results indicate that the catalytic performance of the catalysts was closely related to the nature of the metal promoters.

pmc-11352894.title: Analysis of Primary Graft Dysfunction (PGD) Risk Factors in Lung Transplantation (LuTx) Patients
pmc-11352894.creator: Michał Jan Kubisa, Małgorzata Edyta Wojtyś, Piotr Lisowski, Dawid Kordykiewicz, Maria Piotrowska, Janusz Wójcik, Jarosław Pieróg, Krzysztof Safranow, Tomasz Grodzki, Bartosz Kubisa, Said Dermime
pmc-11352894.description: Background: Primary graft dysfunction (PGD) is a form of acute lung injury (ALI) that occurs within 72 h after lung transplantation (LuTx) and is the most common early complication of the procedure. PGD is diagnosed and graded based on the ratio of the partial pressure of arterial oxygen to the fraction of inspired oxygen and chest X-ray results.

pmc-11511039.description: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are a promising technology for sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks. However, a fully passive RIS cannot independently process signals. Wireless systems equipped with it often encounter the challenge of large channel matrix dimensions when acquiring channel state information using pilot-assisted algorithms, resulting in high pilot overhead.

Nevertheless, the specific targets and mechanisms through which ISO exerts its effects against renal interstitial fibrosis (RIF) remain insufficiently explored.

pmc-13392197.title: High SIGLEC10‐Expressing Tumor‐Associated Macrophages Participate in Remodeling the Tumor Immune Microenvironment and Predict Poor Prognosis in Colorectal Cancer
pmc-13392197.creator: Chuang Miao, Fei Qian
pmc-13392197.description: BackgroundSialic acid‐binding immunoglobulin‐like lectin 10 (SIGLEC10), a member of the SIGLEC family, is selectively expressed on multiple immune cell subsets and plays a key role in immune regulation through the recognition of sialylated ligands. Recent studies suggest that SIGLEC10 functions as an emerging immune checkpoint that contributes to the regulation of tumor‐associated macrophages (TAMs) within the tumor microenvironment (TME).

pmc-13537796.title: Combined inulin and glucomannan modulate colonic cytokine balance and mucosal barrier function in a western diet-induced colonic inflammation mouse model
pmc-13537796.creator: Bernadette Dian Novita, Steven Christian Angkawijaya, I Gede Putu Adhi Wedharga, Suciatuz Zinanir Rohman, Ferdinand Wiliam Jaya, Daniella Widarma, David Timothy Abraham, Irene Lingkan Parengkuan, Adi Pramono Hendrata, Hendy Wijaya, Yudy Tjahjono, Sianty Dewi, Niluh Suwasanti, Endang Isbandiati Soedi
pmc-13537796.description: A rising worldwide health concern, inflammatory bowel disease is linked to western-style diets that damage intestinal barrier integrity, change gut microbiota, and increase colonic inflammation. In contrast, inulin and glucomannan enhance short-chain fatty acid production and preserve mucosal structure, suggesting a protective role against diet-induced colonic inflammation.

However, it remains unclear how recommendations on lifestyle interventions are part of CPGs.
